title: the heartbeat spawns device pulses windowless on Windows whatever its own interpreter
intention: Each beat's pulse child on Windows runs windowless (pythonw plus detached_kwargs), even when the loop itself was started under python.exe, so a mis-started loop cannot flash a console every beat.
why: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/heartbeat.py:146 spawns pulses with [sys.executable, path]. Under a python.exe loop sys.executable is python.exe, and each pulse would get its own conhost, a window per beat, which matches the recurring pop-ups Akien reported 2026-11-16 on akienlivingroom. HYPOTHESIS (Law 3): the repeated pop-ups and their stop are measured; that each pulse owned a conhost is not, so the proof must red first. __main__.py:120's os.execv(sys.executable, ...) re-exec has the same shape. Fields drafted by akienlivingroom_cc_0, 2026-11-17.
traces_to: CP4 (the box serves him: his media box); Law 3 (the conhost-per-pulse cause is a labelled hypothesis until the red-first proof measures it).
how: On nt, heartbeat's pulse spawn uses windowless_spawn.background_pythonw() instead of sys.executable, with the tool's detached kwargs; off nt it is unchanged.

clauses.claim: on Windows, with the loop running under python.exe, a beat's pulse child is pythonw.exe and owns no conhost
off Windows the pulse argv is unchanged
the pulse still runs and its result is recorded as before

decisions.text: D1: heartbeat's pulse Popen takes its interpreter from windowless_spawn.background_pythonw() on nt; sys.executable elsewhere.
D2: the proof drives one beat with os_name nt and executable python.exe injected, and a real beat off nt, one tooth per clause.

out: __main__.py's execv (a finding for the voyage if the proof shows it)

measured.saw: repeated pop-ups while the python.exe-started loop ran, none after the stop
measured.how: Akien's report on akienlivingroom, plus Get-CimInstance Win32_Process and Stop-Process
